metadata.title: A unified framework for establishing the universal approximation of transformer-type architectures
metadata.authors: Jingpu Cheng, Ting Lin, Zuowei Shen, Qianxiao Li

nodes.name: Transformer block / hypothesis space $\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$
nodes.statement: A transformer block is $(\operatorname{Id}+h)\circ(\operatorname{Id}+g)$ with $g\in\mathcal{G}$ token-mixing and $h\in\mathcal{H}^{\otimes n}$ token-wise; the transformer hypothesis space $\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ is the set of finite compositions of such blocks.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines a transformer as a composition of blocks alternating token-mixing and token-wise feedforward maps.

nodes.name: $G$-equivariance
nodes.statement: For $G\le S_n$ acting on $\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}$ by token permutation, $f$ is $G$-equivariant if $f(\sigma(X))=\sigma(f(X))$ for all $\sigma\in G$ and all $X$.

nodes.name: $G$-Universal Approximation Property ($G$-UAP)
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ has $G$-UAP in the $L^p$ sense if for every continuous $G$-equivariant $F:\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}$, every compact $K$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $\hat F\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ with $\|\hat F-F\|_{L^p(K)}<\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Nonlinearity and affine-invariance for $\mathcal{H}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{H}$ is nonlinear and affine-invariant if (i) $h\in\mathcal{H},\ W,A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^d \Rightarrow Wh(A\cdot-b)\in\mathcal{H}$, and (ii) $\mathcal{H}$ contains at least one non-affine Lipschitz function.

nodes.name: Token distinguishability for $\mathcal{G}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{G}$ satisfies token distinguishability under $G$-action if for every finite $D=\{X_i\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}$ in general position, there exist $m$ and $g\in(\operatorname{Id}+\mathcal{G})^m$ such that for any $X_i,X_j$ in different $G$-orbits, the tokens of $g(X_i)$ and $g(X_j)$ are all distinct.

nodes.name: Sparsity-pattern adjacency $A_{\mathcal{N}}$ and automorphism $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{N})$
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{N}:[n]\to P([n])$, $A_{\mathcal{N}}(i,j)=1$ iff $j\in\mathcal{N}(i)$; $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{N})=\{\sigma\in S_n\mid j\in\mathcal{N}(i)\Leftrightarrow\sigma(j)\in\mathcal{N}(\sigma(i))\}$.

nodes.name: Sparse transformer family $\mathcal{T}^{\Phi}_{\mathcal{H}}$
nodes.statement: For a sequence $\Phi=(\mathcal{N}_1,\mathcal{N}_2,\ldots)$ of sparsity patterns, $\mathcal{T}^{\Phi}_{\mathcal{H}}$ is the family of finite compositions $(\operatorname{Id}+h_n)\circ(\operatorname{Id}+g_n)\circ\cdots\circ(\operatorname{Id}+h_1)\circ(\operatorname{Id}+g_1)$ with $g_i\in\mathcal{G}_{\mathcal{N}_i}$.

nodes.name: Connectivity within $m$ layers
nodes.statement: $\Phi$ is connected within $m$ layers if for any $i\neq j\in[n]$ there exist $1\le r_1<r_2<\cdots<r_k\le m$ with $A_{\mathcal{N}_{r_k}}A_{\mathcal{N}_{r_{k-1}}}\cdots A_{\mathcal{N}_{r_1}}(i,j)>0$.

nodes.name: Main UAP theorem for transformer-type architectures
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{H}$ is nonlinear and affine-invariant and $\mathcal{G}$ satisfies the token distinguishability condition, then $\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ has the $G$-UAP.

nodes.name: Analytic reduction to two-sample condition
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{G}=\{X\mapsto g(X;\theta)\mid\theta\in\Theta\}$ with $\Theta$ connected open and $\theta\mapsto g(X;\theta)$ analytic for fixed $X$, and $\mathcal{G}$ can distinguish tokens of any 2-element dataset using finitely many layers, then $\mathcal{G}$ satisfies the token distinguishability condition; if a uniform $m$ works for $|D|=2$, the same $m$ works for any finite $D$, and $m$ token-mixing layers plus enough feedforward layers achieve UAP.
assumptions: $\mathcal{G}$ is a parametric family analytic in $\theta$ over a connected open $\Theta$
$\mathcal{G}$ distinguishes tokens of any two-element dataset $D$
conclusions: $\mathcal{G}$ satisfies the full token distinguishability condition
Uniform $m$ for $|D|=2$ implies the same $m$ suffices for any finite $D$

nodes.name: Interpolation property of $\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of TP465.1 and any $G$-equivariant continuous $F$, for any $\varepsilon>0$ and finite $\{X_i\}$, there exists $\hat F\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ with $\|\hat F(X_i)-F(X_i)\|_2<\varepsilon$ when $X_i$ is in general position, and $\|\hat F(X_i)\|_2<n\max_i\{\|F(X_i)\|_2\}+2\varepsilon$ otherwise.
assumptions: $\mathcal{H}$ nonlinear and affine-invariant; $\mathcal{G}$ satisfies token distinguishability under $G$
conclusions: Pointwise $\varepsilon$-interpolation on general-position samples and bounded value control on degenerate samples

nodes.name: Approximation of tensor-type functions
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of TP465.1, for any continuous increasing $h:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $F\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ with $\|F-h^{(d\times n)}\|_{C(K)}\le\varepsilon$, where $h^{(d\times n)}$ acts coordinate-wise.

nodes.name: ResNet interpolation property (corollary of Cheng–Lin–Shen–Li 2025)
nodes.statement: If $d\ge 2$ and $\mathcal{H}$ is nonlinear and affine-invariant, then $\{(\operatorname{Id}+f_k)\circ\cdots\circ(\operatorname{Id}+f_1)\}$ can $\varepsilon$-interpolate any finite dataset $\{(x_i,y_i)\}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d$ with distinct $x_i$.

nodes.name: UAP for kernel-based attention (Theorem on kernel attention)
nodes.statement: If the kernel $k:\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^+$ is analytic and for every $x\neq 0$ and distinct $y_1,y_2\neq 0$, for almost all $W_K$, $\lim_{t\to\infty} k(x,tW_Ky_1)/k(x,tW_Ky_2)\in\{0,\infty\}$, then a transformer with this kernel attention has $S_n$-UAP, and one token-mixing layer with sufficiently many feedforward layers suffices.
assumptions: Almost-all-$W_K$ scaling-limit dichotomy condition holds for distinct nonzero key vectors
conclusions: One token-mixing layer plus enough feedforward layers achieves UAP

nodes.name: UAP for sparse attention transformers
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ is connected within $m$ layers, then $\mathcal{T}^{\Phi}_{\mathcal{H}}$ has $G$-UAP with $G=\bigcap_{i=1}^{\infty}\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{N}_i)$; moreover $m$ attention layers plus sufficiently many feedforward layers achieve the UAP.
assumptions: Kernel $k$ satisfies CP465.1 conditions; $\mathcal{H}$ satisfies DP465.4
conclusions: $m$ attention layers plus enough FFN layers suffice

nodes.name: UAP for LinFormer and SkyFormer
nodes.statement: (i) LinFormer satisfies UAP without symmetric restriction; (ii) SkyFormer satisfies $S_n$-UAP.
assumptions: Attention defined as in (eq:linformer) for LinFormer or (eq:skyformer) for SkyFormer

nodes.name: Sparse-attention UAP for new attention with bias term
nodes.section: 5.1 New attention mechanism with bias term
nodes.statement: Replacing the kernel attention in CP465.2 with the bias-term attention $[\operatorname{Atten}(X)]_i=[X]_i+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{N}(i)} a\,\alpha(W[X]_j-b)$ (with $\alpha$ of polynomial growth, non-polynomial), the same connectivity-based $G$-UAP conclusion holds for $\tilde{\mathcal{T}}^{\Phi}_{\mathcal{H}}$.
assumptions: $\alpha$ has polynomial growth and is not a polynomial

nodes.name: $D_n$- and $C_n$-UAP architectures
nodes.section: 5.2 Transformer with UAP under specific symmetry
nodes.statement: The token-mixing designs proposed for $D_n$ (sliding-window on a cycle with sparsity $\mathcal{N}(i)=\{(i+j)\bmod n: -w\le j\le w\}$) and $C_n$ (column-wise circular convolution $\psi*X$) satisfy token distinguishability under $D_n$ and $C_n$ respectively; combined with a nonlinear affine-invariant $\mathcal{H}$ they yield $D_n$-UAP and $C_n$-UAP.
assumptions: $D_n$ design: kernel $k$ or $\alpha$ satisfies CP465.1/CP465.4 hypotheses; $w\le\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor-1$

nodes.name: Equality-of-attention lemma
nodes.statement: For a kernel $k$ satisfying CP465.1, if two attention outputs from token sequences $\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}$ and $\{b_1,\ldots,b_s\}$ at indices $r',s'$ coincide for all $W_Q,W_K,W_V$, then $r=s$ and there exists $\sigma\in S_n$ with $\sigma(r')=s'$ and $a_i=b_{\sigma(i)}$ for all $i$.
assumptions: Equality of kernel-attention outputs holds for all $W_Q,W_K,W_V$

nodes.name: Auxiliary scaling-limit ordering lemma
nodes.statement: For $\{x_1,\ldots,x_p\}=\{a_i\}\cup\{b_j\}$, there exist $W_K\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ and $\sigma\in S_p$ such that $\lim_{t\to\infty}\tilde k(tW_Kx_{\sigma(j)})/\tilde k(tW_Kx_{\sigma(i)})=\infty$ for all $i<j$.
conclusions: Existence of $W_K$ and total-ordering permutation of the kernel limits

nodes.name: LinFormer equality-of-attention lemma
nodes.statement: If LinFormer outputs at indices $i_1,i_2$ coincide for all $W_Q,W_K,W_V,E,F$ on inputs $X,Y$ in general position, then $i_1=i_2$ and $X=Y$.
assumptions: Equality of LinFormer outputs holds for all parameters

nodes.name: Proof of TP465.1 (main UAP theorem)
nodes.statement: Reduce $G$-UAP to interpolation (PrP465.1) plus tensor-type approximation (PrP465.2); discretize $K=[-s,s]^{d\times n}$ on a grid, build piecewise-constant target $\tilde F$, build $\bar F$ matching $F$ on grid points and $H_{\alpha,\delta}$ approximating the contracting map $h_{\alpha,\delta}^{(d\times n)}$; combine via triangle inequality with each error term $\le\varepsilon/4$.

nodes.name: Piecewise-constant approximation of $F$
nodes.statement: Pick $\delta>0$ with $\tilde F=\sum_{\mathbf{i}}F(\bm p_{\mathbf{i}})\chi_{\mathbf{i},\delta}$ satisfying $\|F-\tilde F\|_{L^p(K)}\le\varepsilon/4$ by uniform continuity of $F$.

nodes.name: Apply interpolation to grid points
nodes.statement: Apply PrP465.3 (interpolation for $(\operatorname{Id}+\mathcal{H})^*$ via PrP465.1 on the grid) to obtain $\bar F\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ with $\|\bar F(\bm p_{\mathbf{i}})-F(\bm p_{\mathbf{i}})\|<\gamma$ on general-position grid corners and bounded otherwise.

nodes.name: Approximate the contracting tensor-type map
nodes.statement: Define the piecewise-linear contraction $h_{\alpha,\delta}$ with cube collapses; by PrP465.2, choose $H_{\alpha,\delta}\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ with $\|H_{\alpha,\delta}-h_{\alpha,\delta}^{(d\times n)}\|_{C(K)}<\rho$.

nodes.name: Bound composition error and conclude
nodes.statement: Split $K=K_1^{\alpha}\cup K_2^{\alpha}\cup(K\setminus K^{\alpha})$, bound each piece by $\varepsilon/4$ using $\gamma,\delta,\alpha,\rho$ chosen sufficiently small/close to 1, and conclude $\|\bar F\circ H_{\alpha,\delta}-F\|_{L^p(K)}<\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP465.2 (analytic two-sample reduction)
nodes.statement: By contradiction: if token distinguishability fails for $N$ samples, the analytic function $\Pi_{i,j}=\prod_{l_1,l_2}\|[g(X_i)]_{l_1}-[g(X_j)]_{l_2}\|_2^2$ in $\theta$ vanishes identically; since the zero set of a nontrivial real-analytic function has measure zero, this forces failure already on a 2-element subset.

nodes.name: Encode failure as analytic identity
nodes.statement: Express token-collision-for-some-pair as $\Pi_{i,j}(\theta)=\prod_{l_1,l_2}\|[g(X_i)]_{l_1}-[g(X_j)]_{l_2}\|_2^2=0$ for all $\theta\in\Theta$.

nodes.name: Invoke measure-zero zero set of analytic functions
nodes.statement: Since $\Pi_{i,j}$ is analytic in $\theta$ on connected open $\Theta$, vanishing on a positive-measure set forces $\Pi_{i,j}\equiv 0$ for some $(i,j)$, giving failure on a two-sample subset; the same $m$ transfers from $|D|=2$ to general $|D|$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP465.1 (kernel UAP)
nodes.statement: Apply LP465.1 to obtain token distinguishability over inputs with non-zero tokens (a full-measure subset); since the failure set has measure zero, $S_n$-UAP follows by the same argument as TP465.1.

nodes.name: Proof of CP465.2 (sparse-attention UAP)
nodes.statement: By contradiction: suppose tokens $[X]_{i_1}$ and $[Y]_{i_2}$ cannot be distinguished by any $g\in\mathcal{G}^{\Phi}_m$; iteratively apply LP465.1 along the connectivity hops to construct a permutation $\sigma\in\bigcap_i\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{N}_i)=G$ with $[X]_i=[Y]_{\sigma(i)}$, contradicting that $X,Y$ are in different $G$-orbits.

nodes.name: Single-layer reduction at hop 1
nodes.statement: Restrict $g$ to one layer $\operatorname{Id}+\mathcal{G}_{\mathcal{N}_{p_1}}$; by LP465.1 applied to the resulting attention identity, the multisets $\{[X]_q:q\in\mathcal{N}_{p_1}(i_1)\}$ and $\{[Y]_q:q\in\mathcal{N}_{p_1}(i_2)\}$ are equal.

nodes.name: Propagate equality to neighbours via earlier layers
nodes.statement: For $p_2<p_1$ and any $g\in\operatorname{Id}+\mathcal{G}_{\mathcal{N}_{p_2}}$, show $[g(X)]_{q_1}=[g(Y)]_{q_2}$; otherwise scale $W_V$ small to get a $g_1$ with $[g_1(X)]_{q_1}\neq[g_1(Y)]_{q_2}$ and apply LP465.1 to a two-layer composition, contradiction.

nodes.name: Iterate over hops up to depth $m$
nodes.statement: Repeat the argument: tokens reachable in $\le m$ hops match. Connectivity within $m$ ensures all indices in $[n]$ are covered, yielding a unique permutation $\sigma$ with $[X]_i=[Y]_{\sigma(i)}$.

nodes.name: Show $\sigma\in G$ to reach contradiction
nodes.statement: Apply LP465.1 once more on each $\mathcal{N}_p$ to deduce $j\in\mathcal{N}_p(i)\Leftrightarrow\sigma(j)\in\mathcal{N}_p(\sigma(i))$, so $\sigma\in\bigcap_p\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{N}_p)=G$, contradicting that $X,Y$ are in different $G$-orbits.

nodes.name: Proof of CP465.4 (bias-term sparse-attention UAP)
nodes.statement: If distinguishability fails, derive an identity $\sum_l c_l\alpha(Wx_l-b)=0$ for all $W,b$; take Fourier transform in $b$ to get $(\sum_l c_l e^{i(Wx_l)^{\top}\xi})\hat\alpha(\xi)=0$; non-polynomial $\alpha$ gives $\hat\alpha\not\equiv 0$ on a non-zero point, leading to a contradiction following Theorem 1 of Cheng et al. 2025.

nodes.name: Proof that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{N})=D_n$ for the cyclic-window pattern
nodes.statement: Show $D_n\le\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{N})$ from cyclic and reflection symmetry; conversely use $|\mathcal{N}(1)\cap\mathcal{N}(j)|=2w$ to identify $\gamma(2)\in\{2,n\}$ and propagate, concluding $\gamma$ is identity or reflection $(2,n)(3,n-1)\cdots$.

nodes.name: Two-step transformer block
nodes.statement: $X_{t+1/2}=X_t+\operatorname{Atten}(X_t),\quad X_{t+1}=X_{t+1/2}+\operatorname{FFN}(X_{t+1/2})$.

nodes.name: Original softmax attention
nodes.statement: $\operatorname{Atten}(X_t)=\sum_{i=1}^N W_V^{t,i}X_t\,\operatorname{softmax}((W_K^{t,i}X_t)^{\top}W_Q^{t,i}X_t)$.

nodes.name: Kernel-based attention
nodes.statement: $[\operatorname{Atten}(X)]_i=\frac{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{N}(i)} k([W_QX]_i,[W_KX]_j)[W_VX]_j}{\sum_{j\in\mathcal{N}(i)} k([W_QX]_i,[W_KX]_j)}$.

nodes.name: LinFormer attention
nodes.statement: $\operatorname{Atten}(X)=W_V^t X F\operatorname{softmax}((W_K^t X E)^{\top} W_Q^t X)$, with $E,F\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$.

nodes.name: SkyFormer kernelized attention
nodes.statement: $[\operatorname{Atten}(X)]_i=\sum_{j=1}^n \exp(-\tfrac12\|[W_QX]_i-[W_KX]_j\|^2)W_V X_j$.

nodes.name: New attention with bias term
nodes.statement: $[\operatorname{Atten}(X)]_i=[X]_i+\sum_{j\in\mathcal{N}(i)} a\,\alpha(W[X]_j-b)$, with $\alpha$ of polynomial growth.

nodes.name: Circular column-wise convolution
nodes.statement: $[\psi*X]_i=\sum_{j=0}^{l}\psi_j[X]_{(i+j)\bmod n}$ for $i=0,\ldots,n-1$, with trainable $\psi\in\mathbb{R}^{l+1}$.

nodes.name: Concrete kernels satisfying CP465.1 (softmax, RBF, Performer, sum-exp, polynomial-modulated)
nodes.statement: $k(x,y)=\exp(x^{\top}y)$ (original transformer); $k(x,y)=\exp(-\gamma\|x-y\|_2^2)$ (RBF, Tsai 2019); $k(x,y)=\phi(x)^{\top}\phi(y)$ with random Gaussian features (Performer); $k(x,y)=\exp(w^{\top}(x+y))$; $k(x,y)=p(x-y)\tilde k(x,y)$ with $p$ positive polynomial — all satisfy the kernel UAP condition (the Performer case almost surely).

nodes.name: Sparse patterns covered by CP465.2
nodes.statement: Periodic switching between fixed and strided attention (Child et al. 2019); sliding-window with optional global seeds (Longformer, Beltagy 2020); star-shape attention (Guo 2019); BigBird mixture of windows, global seeds and random connections (Zaheer 2020).

nodes.name: $D_n$- and $C_n$-symmetric architectures
nodes.statement: $D_n$ design: kernel/$\alpha$-attention with sparsity $\mathcal{N}(i)=\{(i+j)\bmod n:-w\le j\le w\}$, $w\le\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor-1$. $C_n$ design: token-mixing via column-wise circular convolution $\psi*X$. Applications include molecular structure (dihedral) and periodic time series / variable-star classification (cyclic).

nodes.name: Positional encoding bridges $G$-UAP to general UAP
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}$ has $G$-UAP for some $G$, then for any compact $K$ there exists a fixed positional encoding $\operatorname{Enc}:X\mapsto X+E$ such that $\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{G},\mathcal{H}}\circ\operatorname{Enc}$ approximates any continuous function on $K$ in $L^p$, by making each token-position domain distinct.

nodes.name: Random sparse patterns are typically asymmetric
nodes.statement: By Erdős–Rényi-type results on graph automorphisms, when $n$ is large a random sparse pattern $\mathcal{N}$ has trivial automorphism group with probability tending to 1, so most connected sparse patterns yield UAP without symmetric restriction even without positional encodings.

nodes.name: Limitations: normalization, non-analytic attentions, quantitative rates
nodes.statement: The framework omits normalization layers; attentions like Katharopoulos 2020 do not satisfy the analyticity assumption of TP465.2; the non-constructive criteria do not yield quantitative rates separating contributions of components such as multi-head attention, mixture-of-experts, or low-rank projections.

nodes.name: Universal interpolation for Lipschitz residual networks (Cheng–Lin–Shen–Li 2025)
nodes.statement: For $d\ge 2$, if $\mathcal{H}$ is nonlinear and affine-invariant, then $(\operatorname{Id}+\mathcal{H})^*$ has the universal interpolation property and approximates any continuous function $\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ in $L^p$ on compacta.
nodes.origin_citation: Cheng, Lin, Shen, Li 2025 (Theorem 2.6 / Proposition 4.11 of Li et al. 2022)

nodes.name: Zero set of a non-trivial real-analytic function has measure zero
nodes.statement: If $f:\Theta\to\mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic on a connected open $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ and not identically zero, then $\{f=0\}$ has Lebesgue measure zero.

nodes.name: Original-transformer UAP (Yun et al. 2019, 2020)
nodes.statement: Transformers with softmax attention are universal approximators of fixed-length sequence-to-sequence functions on compact domains, established constructively via contextual mappings.

nodes.name: BigBird sparse-transformer UAP (Zaheer et al. 2020)
nodes.statement: Transformers with the BigBird sparse attention pattern (sliding window + global tokens + random connections) are universal sequence-to-sequence approximators.

nodes.name: Single-attention-layer transformer memorization / UAP (Kajitsuka & Sato)
nodes.statement: Transformers with a single attention layer and sufficiently deep feedforward networks achieve UAP and have characterized memorization capacity for finite datasets.

nodes.name: Symmetric-function UAP under transitive subgroups (Li et al. 2024)
nodes.statement: Deep neural networks satisfy a sufficient condition for universal approximation of symmetric (equivariant) functions when the group action is by a transitive subgroup of $S_n$ acting on coordinates.

nodes.name: Erdős–Rényi asymmetry of random graphs
nodes.statement: Almost every finite simple graph on $n$ vertices is asymmetric (trivial automorphism group) as $n\to\infty$.
